title: Stored Energy and Electricity
seo_title: Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology: Stored Energy and Electricity Worksheets (NERDC)
standard_code: Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology: You and Energy
standard_text: Fuels such as wood, coal, paraffin and gas store energy that is released when they burn. Cells (batteries) store energy for electrical circuits. Electricity is generated in power stations; we must use it safely and save energy. (summary of the Basic Science and Technology curriculum, Primary 6, theme: You and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Primary 6 Basic Science and Technology worksheets (NERDC curriculum, theme: You and Energy): energy changes, renewable and non-renewable, electrical appliances, simple circuits and saving energy. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Fuels store energy that is released when they burn.
key_sub: A circuit needs a complete loop.
body_html:
How to think about it

A fuel is a material that stores energy, which is released as heat and light when it burns: wood, coal, paraffin, petrol and gas. Burning needs air. Fuels must be used safely, because fires and fumes (carbon monoxide) are dangerous.

Cells (batteries) store energy that can make electricity flow. A simple circuit needs a cell, wires and a bulb joined in a complete loop; a switch opens and closes the loop. Most of Nigeria's electricity comes from natural gas power stations and hydroelectric dams such as Kainji, so saving electricity also saves fuel.

Example

A bulb does not light. The wire is not connected to the cell. Why?

Is the loop complete?

Answer: the circuit is not complete

Example

What does a fuel need to burn?

A candle under a jar goes out.

Answer: air (oxygen)

Common mistakes

  • Thinking a circuit works with one wire.
  • Thinking batteries make energy from nothing.
  • Using a gas or paraffin heater in a closed room.

faq.q: Why should you never burn coal or paraffin in a closed room?
faq.a: It uses up oxygen and makes poisonous carbon monoxide gas.

faq.q: How can a family save electricity?
faq.a: Switch off lights and appliances, use energy-saving bulbs and a solar geyser.

items.q: Which action saves energy at home?
c: opening windows with the heat on
turning off lights when you leave a room
leaving the TV on all night
items.e: Small actions add up.

items.q: A stretched elastic band stores which form of energy?
items.e: It is released when let go.

items.q: A toy car with a motor changes electric energy into which main form of energy?
c: electric energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of a toy car with a motor is to make motion.

items.q: Which device changes electric energy into heat?
items.e: Look at what goes in (electric energy) and what comes out (heat).

items.q: Which device changes electric energy into light?

items.e: Look at what goes in (electric energy) and what comes out (light).

items.q: Which is a non-renewable energy source?
items.e: Fossil fuels took millions of years to form.

items.q: A toaster changes electric energy into which main form of energy?

items.q: A catapult shoots a stone. Which shows the main energy conversion?
items.e: A catapult shoots a stone: elastic potential energy → kinetic energy.

items.q: A candle burns. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → light energy and heat energy
light energy and heat energy → chemical potential energy
items.e: A candle burns: chemical potential energy → light energy and heat energy.

items.q: Water flows down from a dam and turns a generator. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy
gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy
electrical energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy
items.e: Water flows down from a dam and turns a generator: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy → electrical energy.

items.q: A ball falls from a table to the floor. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → kinetic energy → gravitational potential energy
items.e: A ball falls from a table to the floor: gravitational potential energy → kinetic energy.

items.q: Which device changes electric energy into sound?

items.e: Look at what goes in (electric energy) and what comes out (sound).

c: electric energy only, with no change
items.e: The main job of a speaker is to make sound.

items.e: The main job of a torch is to make light.

items.q: A wound-up toy car runs across the floor. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → light energy and heat energy
items.e: A wound-up toy car runs across the floor: elastic potential energy → kinetic energy.

items.q: A battery powers a torch. Which shows the main energy conversion?
c: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy
light energy → electrical energy → chemical potential energy
items.e: A battery powers a torch: chemical potential energy → electrical energy → light energy.

items.q: Which is a renewable energy source?
items.e: Wind will not run out.

items.q: Which device changes electric energy into heat?

items.e: Look at what goes in (electric energy) and what comes out (heat).

items.e: Look at what goes in (electric energy) and what comes out (motion).

items.q: Kelechi reads about a resource that formed from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries. Which resource is it?
items.e: That is how copper and gold ores formed.

items.q: People use a coal power station to get energy from coal. Which is a benefit of this energy source?
c: It can make electricity day and night.
It is replaced naturally in a few days.
items.e: It can make electricity day and night.

items.q: Why should you put on a sweater instead of turning up the heat?
c: It makes the house warmer for everyone.
items.e: Conserving energy reduces pollution.

items.q: What does 'reduce, reuse, recycle' help save?
c: resources and the energy needed to make new things
items.e: Making new products uses energy.

items.q: People use petrol in cars to get energy from oil. Which is a problem with this energy source?
c: It only works in places with hot rock near the surface.
Turbines can harm birds and bats, and they need steady wind.
A dam floods land and blocks fish from swimming up the river.
Burning petrol pollutes the air, and oil spills harm ocean life.
items.e: Burning petrol pollutes the air, and oil spills harm ocean life.

items.q: People use a gas stove or gas power station to get energy from natural gas. Which is a benefit of this energy source?
c: It is replaced naturally in a few days.
It can make electricity day and night.
items.e: It can make electricity day and night.

items.q: Which energy source is not renewable?
items.e: Natural gas formed over millions of years and will run out; burning it also pollutes the air.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?
items.e: Sunlight is renewed by nature and does not run out. Coal, oil and gas take millions of years to form.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?

items.q: What is a disadvantage of burning fossil fuels?

items.e: Fossil fuels add greenhouse gases.

It makes no air pollution while working.

It makes new energy from nothing.
items.e: It makes no air pollution while working.

items.q: Why are LED bulbs better than old incandescent bulbs?
c: They give the same light using much less electricity.
They are brighter only because they are hot.
items.e: Less energy is wasted as heat.

items.q: Which energy source is renewable?

items.q: Which energy source is not renewable?

items.q: Nonso asks how copper and gold ores formed. What is the best explanation?
c: from plants from ancient swamps buried and squeezed for millions of years
from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries
from tiny marine organisms buried in ocean sediments, then heated and pressed for millions of years
from seawater evaporating in shallow basins long ago
items.e: Copper and gold ores formed from hot, mineral-rich water and magma near volcanoes and plate boundaries.

items.q: Which is used to turn oil (as petrol) into electricity or motion?
items.e: Energy from oil is used with petrol in cars.

items.q: What does a switch do in a circuit?
c: It pushes electricity around the circuit.
It opens or closes a gap to turn the circuit off or on.
It lights up when electricity flows through it.
It makes a sound when electricity flows through it.
items.e: Each part has a job.

items.q: Which of these needs electricity to work: a TV remote control, a book, a skipping rope or scissors?
items.e: Electrical appliances need electricity from the mains or a battery.

items.q: Two wires go from a bulb, but both are joined to the same end of the cell. Will the bulb light?
c: No, the loop does not go through the cell.
No, there is only one wire, so the circuit is not complete.
Yes, the circuit is a complete loop.
No, the loose wire leaves a gap.
items.e: A bulb lights only in a complete loop with a cell.

items.q: Which of these needs electricity to work: a book, a skipping rope, an oven or scissors?
items.e: Electrical appliances need electricity from the mains or a battery.

items.q: A bulb, a cell and a switch are joined in a loop, and the switch is closed. Will the bulb light?
c: No, there is only one wire, so the circuit is not complete.
No, the open switch makes a gap.
No, there is nothing to push the electricity.
Yes, the circuit is a complete loop.
items.e: A bulb lights only in a complete loop with a cell.

items.q: Hauwa draws this circuit. Will the lamp light up?
c: No, the switch is open so there is a gap.
No, there is a gap in the wire.
No, there is no cell to push the current.
Yes, the loop is complete and the switch is closed.
items.e: A component works only in a complete loop with a cell and no gaps.

items.q: In Chidi's circuit, the left switch is closed and the right switch is closed. Will the lamp light up?

No, two switches can never work together.
No, at least one switch is open.
items.e: With two switches in one loop, both must be closed for current to flow.

items.q: A lamp in a circuit will not light. A wire has come off one side of the lamp holder. What is the most likely reason?
c: Plastic is an insulator, so it blocks the current.
One cell is flat, so there is not enough voltage.
There is a gap, so the circuit is not complete.
items.e: Check: cells, bulb, every connection, switches and materials.

items.q: A forest is cut down and animals lose their homes. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Add rubbish and recycling bins and hold clean-up days.
Plant cover crops and rows of trees to hold the soil.
Build wind turbines and solar panels.
Replant trees and protect part of the forest as a park.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Replant trees and protect part of the forest as a park.

items.q: Which of the three R's is turning off lights in empty rooms?
items.e: Reducing means using less in the first place.

items.q: A city's air is smoggy from car exhaust. Which solution best addresses this problem?
c: Leave strips of plants along the water and use less fertiliser.
Add bus lines and bike lanes so fewer people drive.
Add rubbish and recycling bins and hold clean-up days.
items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Add bus lines and bike lanes so fewer people drive.

items.q: An old bulb uses 40 watts and an LED bulb that gives the same light uses 6 watts. A school replaces 6 old bulbs with LEDs. How many fewer watts are used when they are all on?
items.e: (40 − 6) × 6 = 204 watts. Using less electricity means less fuel burned at power stations.

items.q: Fertiliser runoff makes algae grow over a pond. Which solution best addresses this problem?

Build wind turbines and solar panels.

items.e: This solution deals with the cause of the problem. Leave strips of plants along the water and use less fertiliser.

items.q: Which of the three R's is turning an old jar into a pencil holder?
items.e: Reusing means using something again for the same or a new job.

items.q: A beach is covered with litter after summer weekends. Which solution best addresses this problem?

items.q: Which of the three R's is turning off the water while brushing your teeth?
items.e: Reducing means using less in the first place.
